policy_name: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 Information technology — Artificial intelligence — Management system
issuing_authority: ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 42 (International Organization for Standardization and International Electrotechnical Commission)
regulatory_regime: Voluntary international management system standard (certifiable via accredited certification bodies)
geo_constraints: None; applies to any organization that adopts it

locale_context.regulation: Voluntary standard · certifiable AI management system
locale_context.culture: International standards culture: process- and management-system oriented (Plan-Do-Check-Act), certification-driven; global but EU/industry uptake strongest.

key_dates.event: Supporting standards ISO/IEC 42005:2025 (AI system impact assessment) and ISO/IEC 42006:2025 (requirements for certification bodies) published
Reported CEN approval of EN ISO/IEC 42001:2026 (European adoption) — secondary source, unverified

covered_entities: any organization, regardless of size, type or nature, that provides or uses products or services utilizing AI systems
covered_systems: AI systems developed, provided or used by the organization
covered_activities: establishing, implementing, maintaining and continually improving an AI management system (AIMS)
conditions: Conformity requires meeting all requirements of Clauses 4–10; exclusion of Annex A controls must be justified in the Statement of Applicability
objective: Specify requirements for establishing, implementing, maintaining and continually improving an AI management system within an organization, so that AI systems are developed, provided or used responsibly in pursuit of the organization's objectives and in line with stakeholder expectations.
conflict_rule: Voluntary standard; legal and regulatory requirements are to be determined as part of the organization's context (Clause 4) and take precedence. Uses the ISO harmonized structure, enabling integration with ISO/IEC 27001 and other management system standards.

sources_consulted: https://www.iso.org/standard/81230.html (catalogue page, via search results only)
Secondary summaries surfaced via web search (e.g. docs.modulos.ai ISO 42001 pages, gaicc.org status page)
record_provenance.notes: Paywalled standard: the official text was not accessed; all clauses are paraphrases (text_is_verbatim=false) based on the standard's well-known clause structure as corroborated by secondary sources. iso.org could not be fetched from this session. Secondary sources (Sept–Oct 2026) report no amendment or revision registered. Exact publication day (believed 18 Dec 2023) not verified, so only YYYY-MM is given. Normative status of Annexes is reported inconsistently in secondary sources; this record treats Annex A (reference control objectives and controls) as normative, which should be checked. Secondary sources count 38 Annex A controls under 9 objectives (A.2–A.10). Official languages: ISO publishes in English and French; French edition availability not verified.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] Top management shall establish an AI policy that is appropriate to the purpose of the organization, provides a framework for setting AI objectives, includes a commitment to meet applicable requirements and a commitment to continual improvement of the AI management system; the policy shall be documented, communicated within the organization and available to interested parties as appropriate.
clauses.requirement: establish a documented AI policy with commitments to applicable requirements and continual improvement
clauses.purpose: set direction and accountability for responsible AI
clauses.applicable_systems: all AI systems within the AIMS scope
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase of harmonized-structure clause; 'shall' requirements are binding only for conformity/certification, hence MUST within the standard's own logic although the standard is voluntary.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] The organization shall define and establish an AI risk assessment process that is informed by its AI policy and objectives, produces consistent, valid and comparable results, identifies risks that could aid or prevent achieving AI objectives, analyses potential consequences to the organization, individuals and societies together with their likelihood, and evaluates and prioritizes risks against risk criteria; documented information on the process shall be retained.
clauses.requirement: run a documented, repeatable AI risk assessment covering consequences for the organization, individuals and society
clauses.affected_asset: individuals, groups, societies and the organization
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems within the AIMS scope
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase; the standard refers to ISO/IEC 23894 for further guidance on AI risk management.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] The organization shall define an AI risk treatment process to select treatment options, determine the necessary controls, compare them with the controls in Annex A to verify that no necessary controls have been omitted, and produce a Statement of Applicability containing the necessary controls and justification for inclusion or exclusion; it shall formulate a risk treatment plan and obtain approval of residual risks from designated management.
clauses.action: select treatments, determine controls, produce Statement of Applicability
clauses.requirement: treat AI risks with controls cross-checked against Annex A and document a Statement of Applicability
clauses.exception: Annex A controls may be excluded with documented justification
clauses.purpose: ensure appropriate controls for identified AI risks
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems within the AIMS scope

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] The organization shall define a process for assessing the potential consequences for individuals or groups of individuals, and for societies, that can result from the development, provision or use of AI systems, taking into account the technical and societal context and applicable jurisdictions; the results shall be documented and considered in the risk assessment.
clauses.object: impacts of AI systems on individuals, groups and societies
clauses.requirement: perform and document AI system impact assessments feeding into risk assessment
clauses.purpose: protect individuals and society from adverse AI impacts
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems within the AIMS scope
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase; operationalized in Clause 8.4 and Annex A.5; detailed guidance in ISO/IEC 42005:2025.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] The organization shall conduct internal audits at planned intervals to provide information on whether the AI management system conforms to the organization's own requirements and to the requirements of the standard, and is effectively implemented and maintained.
clauses.requirement: audit the AIMS at planned intervals
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems within the AIMS scope
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase of harmonized-structure clause common to ISO management system standards.
